title: Copyright and Artificial Intelligence, Part 1: Digital Replicas
supports_claim: The U.S. Copyright Office concluded that the existing patchwork of federal and state law is inadequate for unauthorized digital replicas of a person's voice or likeness and recommended a new federal digital replica right.
limitations: A policy recommendation report, not a court finding; it does not measure how often unauthorized replicas actually occur and covers United States law only.

title: In the Matter of Rytr LLC, FTC File No. 232-3052 (case timeline)
supports_claim: The FTC alleged that a generative AI writing service offered a testimonial and review feature capable of producing detailed reviews containing specifics the user had never supplied, and the case docket shows the 2024 final order was later set aside in 2025.
limitations: The allegations were never adjudicated on the merits and the final order was set aside, so this documents an enforcement theory and procedural history rather than a proven violation or a measured consumer harm rate.

title: Regulatory framework for AI (EU AI Act policy and implementation timeline)
publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Communications Networks, Content and Technology
supports_claim: The EU AI Act imposes transparency obligations on providers and deployers of systems that generate synthetic audio, image or video content, including machine-readable marking of AI-generated output and disclosure of deepfake content.
limitations: A summary policy page rather than the article text; obligation scope, applicable dates and any guidance or standards that refine marking requirements must be confirmed against the Official Journal text and current Commission guidance at release time.

title: Law on Artificial Intelligence No. 134/2025/QH15
publisher: National Assembly of Viet Nam (via vanban.chinhphu.vn)
supports_claim: Viet Nam has a dedicated AI law in force whose implementing instruments define the risk classification scheme and obligations that a synthetic media product placed on the Vietnamese market must be assessed against.
limitations: The classification outcome for a consumer voice-cloning tool is not determined by reading the framework law alone; Decree 142/2026 and the Decision 33/2026 high-risk list must be reviewed by counsel before any status other than uncertain is asserted.

title: Law on Personal Data Protection No. 91/2025/QH15
publisher: National Assembly of Viet Nam (via vanban.chinhphu.vn)
supports_claim: Viet Nam regulates personal data with a heightened regime for sensitive categories, which is the basis for treating a stored voiceprint and facial likeness as sensitive personal data requiring a lawful basis, retention limits and deletion rights.
limitations: Whether a synthetic voice model derived from a sample counts as sensitive personal data or as derived data is a legal question this reading does not settle; Decree 356/2025 detail and counsel review are required.

title: NIST AI 600-1: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework, Generative AI Profile
publisher: U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology
supports_claim: NIST identifies harmful synthetic content, impersonation and information integrity as generative AI risks and lists provenance tracking, disclosure and incident response as suggested management actions.
limitations: Voluntary guidance that suggests control categories without proving any specific control is effective, and it is not a compliance certification for any jurisdiction.

title: Forfeiture order in the AI-generated voice robocall enforcement action (DOC-405811A1)
supports_claim: The FCC imposed a six million US dollar forfeiture on an individual who used an AI-cloned voice of a real, identifiable person in automated calls sent to voters.
limitations: A telecommunications enforcement action in a political-campaign context, not a creator-platform incident; the penalty measures regulatory response and does not quantify how many recipients were actually deceived.

title: Declaratory ruling that AI-generated voices in robocalls are artificial under the TCPA (DOC-400393A1)
supports_claim: The FCC ruled that a voice generated by AI counts as an artificial voice under existing US telephone consumer protection rules, so no new statute was needed to make cloned-voice calls unlawful.
limitations: Applies to telephone calls under one US statute; it says nothing about whether the same synthetic audio is lawful when published as creator content on a video platform.
